rows: Vendor can change pricing on you
slides.note: Our rule: self-host the boring, stable stuff. Pay for the thing that pages you at night.

slides.title: Pick one job, not sixteen

steps.text: Write down the three tools you'd pay for first. Usually a CRM, a support inbox and automation.
Try the open-source one for exactly one of them. One small server is enough.
Run it alongside the paid tool for two weeks. If nobody notices, cancel. If they do, you learned what you're paying for.
Only then pick the next job.

slides.time: Most teams that try all sixteen at once end up back on the paid stack in a month.

slides.text: Open source is not free. It trades a monthly bill for a weekend and a little responsibility. For most things under 20 people, that's a good trade.
